page: Hetzner Cloud cpx22 is an entry-level virtual server instance powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz under the QEMU hypervisor. The instance provides 2 shared x86_64 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores, accompanied by 4.0 GB of system memory (roughly 1.95 GB per core). Modern instruction set extensions are available to guest workloads, including AVX-512 (supporting VNNI and BF16), hardware cryptography acceleration (AES, VAES, SHA-NI), and bit-manipulation extensions. The system includes an 80 GB local NVMe SSD, while discrete GPU acceleration is not provided.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread performance, with the stress-ng single-core score reaching 3016.89, placing it in the upper quartile of comparable configurations. Conversely, aggregate multi-threaded metrics reflect the limitations of a two-core shared configuration: stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores land in the lower quartile. Memory throughput tests indicate reasonable uncached bandwidth, achieving 46.06 GB/sec read and 52.18 GB/sec write for large blocks, although cached throughput and PassMark memory operations reflect entry-tier constraints.

The bundled 80 GB NVMe storage provides high-speed local disk operations without requiring separate network storage volumes. Due to its shared vCPU allocation and modest memory footprint, the instance offers cost-efficient utility for lightweight workloads, including microservices, development environments, edge proxies, CI/CD runners, and staging web servers, but is constrained for sustained parallel compute or memory-intensive database tasks.
description: Hetzner Cloud cpx22 is a budget-oriented virtual instance featuring 2 shared AMD EPYC x86_64 vCPUs clocked at 2.0 GHz, 4.0 GB of system RAM, and 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It incorporates broad instruction set support including AVX-512 vector extensions and cryptographic accelerators (AES, SHA-NI), with no discrete GPU included. In benchmark evaluations, the cpx22 exhibits competitive single-core execution speed, ranking in the top quartile of stress-ng single-core tests, though multi-core capacity and aggregate memory bandwidth are inherently limited by its shared two-core topology. The attached high-speed NVMe storage delivers low-latency disk I/O, rendering the instance a cost-effective platform for lightweight development servers, staging environments, microservices, container hosts, and low-traffic web applications.
